analysis: The supplied changes are documentation and changelog only: changelog.d/landing-agent-documents.md (new), docs/architecture/components/landing.md (lines 30-35, 41, 60) and docs/developer/test.md (lines 985-987). They describe removing the Developers and Contact HTML pages, footer links and sitemap entries from the landing site, while keeping explicit and negotiated Markdown at /developers.md and /contact.md. Browser requests to the retired paths return 404, and human-facing API links point to the official documentation. No executable source, proxy.ts, agent-resources.ts, sitemap.ts or test code is in this batch, so those behaviors are unverified. Checked against the threat model: none of A-001 through A-017, TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-009, TB-011 or the provider, attestation and cache threats (T-041 included) are touched. The documentation introduces no new trust boundary and no secrets, and it claims no authentication, billing or inference behavior (the landing site remains out of scope for the coordinator). The only remaining question is whether the landing code matches the documented 404 and Markdown negotiation, including Vary handling and RSC paths. That is a public-content correctness matter and not a threat-model-relevant regression, and the code is not in this batch.
